setting: A fictional planning meeting, chaired by the learner, for an onboarding workshop.

presentation.situation: You chair a meeting with {{a}} and {{b}} to plan a {{length}}-minute onboarding workshop for {{people}} new colleagues next Friday. Agree an agenda, task owners and preparation steps.
presentation.opening: I'm {{a}}, the project coordinator, and {{b}} is our training facilitator. We're planning a {{length}}-minute onboarding workshop for {{people}} colleagues next Friday. What should they be able to do afterwards?

brief.you_are: You are chairing a planning meeting.
brief.situation: You chair a meeting with {{a}} and {{b}} to plan a {{length}}-minute onboarding workshop for {{people}} new colleagues next Friday. Agree an agenda, task owners and preparation steps.
brief.task: Contribute at least one useful idea, respond to both colleagues, and finish with a decision about the plan.
brief.done_looks_like: There is a shared decision on the agenda and on who does what.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are chairing a planning meeting.
goals: Contribute at least one useful idea, respond to both colleagues, and finish with a decision about the plan.

card.want: An agenda that fits the room booking and the budget.
card.speech: Clear everyday English. Natural, not formal.
tactics: Bring up time and room limits

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

card.want: Enough paired practice so that new colleagues can really do the task.
card.speech: Clear everyday English. Natural, not formal.
tactics: Propose a demonstration and paired practice

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: The workshop is for {{people}} new colleagues next Friday and lasts {{length}} minutes.
The goal is for each new colleague to complete one basic product task independently and know where to ask for help.
The room is available from 09:00 to 11:00 and has one projector.
The workshop must include a product demonstration, paired practice and questions. The spending limit is USD {{budget}}.
{{a}} can arrange the room and send the agenda.
{{b}} suggests a 20-minute demonstration and 40 minutes of paired practice, and can prepare the materials.

objectives.evidence: The learner contributes a useful idea for the plan.
alternatives: I suggest we spend most of the time on paired practice.

objectives.evidence: The learner responds to or invites both speakers.
alternatives: {{a}}, does that fit the room? {{b}}, what do you think?

objectives.evidence: The learner states a shared decision.
alternatives: So we agree: demo first, then paired practice. {{a}} sends the agenda.

beats.goal: Hear an idea from the chair.
opportunity: So what do you suggest we prioritise?
What is your idea for the first part?
beats.orient: You're chairing this planning meeting. Suggest one idea for the workshop. You can say: I suggest we.
fallback: What is your idea for the first part?
So what do you suggest we prioritise?

signals: \b(?:what do you think|do you agree|your view)\b
opportunity: I think the demonstration should be short.
Does that fit the room booking, though?
beats.orient: We each have a view. Ask each of us by name what we think.
fallback: Does that fit the room booking, though?
I think the demonstration should be short.
beats.second_line: I would keep the demonstration short, so people get most of the time for paired practice.

beats.orient: Time to decide. Say what we agree, and who does what. Start with: So we agree.

closing_line: Good. That's a clear plan. Thanks for chairing.

o1.good: Bringing your own idea, with a reason.
common_mistakes: Only asking others what to do
o1.micro_lesson: Say: I suggest we, then: because.
o1.model: I suggest we start with a short demonstration, because people learn by doing.

o2.good: Bringing both people in, by name.
o2.micro_lesson: Ask each person by name: What do you think?
o2.model: {{a}}, does that fit the room? {{b}}, what do you think?

o3.good: Saying the decision out loud so nobody leaves unsure.
o3.micro_lesson: Say: So we agree, and name the owners.
o3.model: So we agree: demonstration first, then paired practice. {{a}} sends the agenda.
